newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Wednesday were seen steady-$1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by continued weakness in pork prices, livestock dealers said.
Lower pork values kept packer operating margins in the red and overwhelmed potential support for hog prices from light movement, the dealers said.

Fresh hams at midday were quoted weak and pork bellies were $3.00 to $5.00 per cwt lower, compared with Monday's close, USDA reported in its central U.S. carlot pork report. The declines offset gains in lean trimmings of mostly $2.00.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog movement on Tuesday was estimated at 100,000 head, compared with 112,000 last week, USDA reported.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant on Wednesday were seen off $0.50 at $59.00, livestock dealers said.
Illinois hog prices at the plant were expected steady to $0.50 lower, peaking in a range of $59.00 to $59.50.
Indiana/Ohio hog top prices for hogs shipped to the plant were seen $1.00 lower at $59.00, the dealers said.
